estimand: region-native annual planning balance under stated demand, resource, and response conditions

resource_conditions.rule: NERC source-published prospective margin path reconstructed on source net demand
shift positive annual net changes in the anticipated resource path by one year; apply negative annual net changes on schedule
shift positive annual net changes in the anticipated resource path by two years; apply negative annual net changes on schedule
shift positive annual net changes in the anticipated resource path by three years; apply negative annual net changes on schedule

response_conditions.rule: ordinary response capped at the first forecast-year quantity; explicit ERCOT provisional large-load curtailment excluded
full response quantity reported in the source table

source_embedded.rule: use the source gross-demand path without adding the author-modeled data-center path

footprint_exclusion.reason: the author-modeled California path is CAISO-based and is not interchangeable with the broader WECC-California planning footprint

headline_scenarios.role: high data-center growth stress with explicit embedded-load envelope
combined high-load, delayed-net-addition, and response-conservative stress

interpretation_boundaries: No scenario is labelled a probabilistic forecast or unique most-likely future.
A negative balance indicates resources below the region-native reference requirement under the stated condition, not an outage forecast.
The modeled low/mid/high paths are fixed-total spatial stress paths and are not automatically additional to official demand forecasts.
For MISO and ERCOT, source-path replacement and linked-response diagnostics govern attribution; generic overlap stresses are consistency tests only.
The timing-stress resource paths delay positive annual net changes, not identified individual projects, and are not project-delivery forecasts.
Unknown data-center attribution remains null and is never converted to zero.
Region-native GW balances are not summed across regions.
